notes:
CIRCUIT: a 5-column x 6-rail hand-drawn ladder of passives, with all five sources stacked in the right-hand column. 14 components, 7 nets, 27 terminals.
Columns (vertical wires, left to right): C1 x~65 [1uH inductor y~117-159, 5uF cap y~337-393]; C2 x~250-275 [5uH inductor y~277-329, 10nF cap y~472-533]; C3 x~475 [10uH inductor y~476-541, 50pF cap y~634-694]; C4 x~628 [50uH inductor y~614-666, 100pF cap y~807-853]; C5 x~845 [V-AC 3V/1kHz, I-AC 5A/1kHz, V-DC 5V, I-DC 10A, V-DC 15V, top to bottom].
Rails (horizontal): H0 top y~62 (x 57..858); H1 y~255 (C1..C5); H2 y~420 (C2..C5); H3 y~570 (C2..C5); H4 y~755 (C3..C5); H5 bottom y~858 (C1..C5, GND stub at x~490).
Drafter's convention on this sheet: a NON-connection is drawn as the VERTICAL wire bowing out to the RIGHT around the horizontal rail; a connection is a plain T, usually with a fat solder blob.

NET MAP:
 n1 = top rail H0, from the top-left corner (x~57) across to x~858 where it turns down into the V-AC. T-joined (solder blobs) by C2 at (275,65), C3 at (496,69), C4 at (638,71). Terminals: 1uH top (0.0), 5uH top (3.0), 10uH top (6.0), 50uH top (9.0), V-AC top (1.1). 5 terminals.
 n2 = rail H1, left end T-ing on C1 at (63,257), right end landing on C5 at (845,261) between the V-AC and the I-AC. C2, C3 and C4 all pass over it without joining. Terminals: 1uH bottom (0.1), 5uF top (4.1), V-AC bottom (1.0), I-AC top (2.0). 4 terminals.
 n3 = rail H2, left end T-ing on C2 at (248,422) (between the 5uH and the 10nF), right end on C5 at (844,428) between the I-AC and the 5V source. C3 and C4 pass over it. Terminals: 5uH bottom (3.1), 10nF top (7.0), I-AC bottom (2.1), V-DC 5V top (5.0). 4 terminals.
 0 = the bottom rail H5 (C1's bottom-left corner across to C5's bottom, carrying the GND stub at (500,860)) UNITED WITH rail H3: C2 runs uninterrupted from H3 at (271,596) straight down to the bottom rail at (279,854), so H3 and the bottom rail are one node. H3's right end lands on C5 at (845,560) between the 5V source and the I-DC; C3 and C4 pass over H3 without joining. Terminals: 5uF bottom (4.0), 10nF bottom (7.1), V-DC 5V bottom (5.1), I-DC top (8.0), 100pF bottom (12.1), V-DC 15V bottom (11.1), GND (13.0). 7 terminals.
 n4 = the stretch of C3 between the 10uH bottom lead and the 50pF top plate; it bows over rail H3 at (476,570). Terminals 6.1, 10.0.
 n5 = rail H4, whose left end is C3's bottom corner at (480,762) (below the 50pF) and whose right end lands on C5 at (841,753) between the I-DC and the 15V source; C4 bows over it at (646,756). Terminals: 50pF bottom (10.1), I-DC bottom (8.1), V-DC 15V top (11.0). 3 terminals.
 n6 = the stretch of C4 between the 50uH bottom lead and the 100pF top plate; it bows over rail H4 at (646,756). Terminals 9.1, 12.0.

JUDGEMENT CALLS:
 * S8/S10, C2 crossing rail H1 at ~(255,251) - the decisive call on this sheet, and the one the tracer got wrong. Unlike the seven clean bows elsewhere, here the drafter drew the detour badly: the column bows right from (265,205) to (271,240), grazes the rail at ~(264,250), and re-enters below the rail through a short left-curving hook to (246,256) before running down to the 5uH. inkmap at (260,250) confirms the column ink above sits at x 261-269 and the column ink below at x 244-249, joined only by a 4px-tall arc that sits UNDER the rail - i.e. the wire steps sideways past the rail rather than terminating on it. The tracer split this into two 3-branch sites (S8 branches = column-above e6 / link e17 / rail-right e18; S10 branches = rail-left e16 / link e17 / column-below e23) and unioned everything. Decided CROSSING, encoded as "8": [[6,17,23],[16,18]] with "10":"none" - the two column halves plus the link form one group, the two rail halves the other. DECISIVE REASON is electrical impossibility, not the ink: C2 is unbroken from the top rail (solder blob T at (275,65)) down to this point, the top rail carries the V-AC's TOP terminal, and rail H1's right end carries the V-AC's BOTTOM terminal via an unmistakable T at (845,261). A junction here shorts the 3V AC source across itself, and also shorts the 1uH inductor (top on H0, bottom on H1). That is what produced the tracer's 14-terminal net 0 containing 0.0+0.1, 1.0+1.1 and 6.0+6.1.
 * S30/S33/S35/S36, C3 over rail H3 at (476,570) - the tracer defaulted all four skeleton fragments to junction. inkmap at (476,570) shows the column at x~470 bowing right to an apex at (483,572) and returning to (469,586) while the rail runs straight through underneath: a textbook hop of exactly the same shape as S9/S11/S21/S23/S42. OVERRIDDEN to a crossing via explicit edge groups on S35: [[59,61,68,73],[64,67,69,70,71]] with "none" on S30/S33/S36. e59 = column above (to the 10uH bottom lead), e73 = column below (to the 50pF top plate), e69/e71 = the two halves of rail H3; e61/e68 are arc fragments, e64/e67/e70 are pen ticks at the rail. Had it been a junction, n4 would have collapsed into net 0 and both the 10uH and the 50pF would have been grounded at both ends.
 * S32/S37/S38, C4 over rail H3 at (632,576) - identical construction, the bow runs (625,560) -> (636,578) -> (627,592). OVERRIDDEN with explicit groups on S38: [[49,62,75],[65,66,71,74]], "none" on S32/S37. A junction would have merged n6 into net 0.
 * S9 (500,252), S11 (650,255), S21 (642,411), S23 (493,418), S42 (646,756) - unambiguous right-hand bows; recorded as crossings, agreeing with the tracer. Reading any as a junction would short a column into a rail and collapse the ladder.
 * S0 (275,65), S3 (496,69), S4 (638,71) - column tops meeting the top rail; each carries a fat blob or pen curl (dot 2.2-2.9). JUNCTIONS.
 * S12 (63,257), S24 (248,422), S39 (271,596) - rail left ends T-ing onto a column that continues through. JUNCTIONS.
 * S13 (845,261), S25 (844,428), S31 (845,560), S41 (841,753), S5 (858,93) - rail right ends landing on the source column C5 between two sources. JUNCTIONS.
 * S47 (279,854), S50 (281,865), S51 (626,866) - column bottoms landing on the bottom rail (the rail has a small step at C2, hence two sites); S49 (500,860) - the GND stub. JUNCTIONS.
